recognize_zh: 低倍視野中散佈多個含細小環狀寄生蟲的紅血球，有些紅血球內含多個蟲體，並見紅血球外的小型蟲體，無瘧色素、裂殖體或配子體，符合巴貝西蟲（Babesia）感染。
features: Scattered red cells containing tiny intraerythrocytic ring and dot forms
Occasional red cells with more than one parasite
Small extracellular forms between red cells (some may be platelets)
No pigment, schizonts or gametocytes; red cells not enlarged
Tetrads not resolvable at this magnification
Partial nucleated cell at the left edge and a few crenated red cells
describe_en: Giemsa-stained peripheral blood smear at low magnification shows scattered red cells containing tiny intraerythrocytic ring and dot forms, with occasional red cells harboring more than one parasite. Small extracellular forms are present between red cells, although some may represent platelets. There is no hemozoin pigment, schizont or gametocyte, and infected red cells are normal in size; tetrad forms cannot be resolved at this power. A partially captured nucleated cell is present at the left edge, and a few crenated red cells are likely artifactual. Findings are consistent with Babesia infection; confirmation by high-power examination and PCR is recommended.

ddx.vs: P. falciparum lacks extracellular forms and tetrads and may show gametocytes, Maurer's clefts or pigment, with a travel history to an endemic area.
Overlying platelets are granular with a halo and are not ring-shaped with a pale central vacuole.
Artifacts are refractile or lie in varied focal planes over cells and background, lacking consistent ring morphology.
